injuries.description: removal of part of the left thumb
source: He was admitted to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital and underwent an operation for the removal of part of the left thumb and part of the left forefinger.
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation of two or more fingers at or near base, left hand

injuries.description: removal of part of the left forefinger
source: He was admitted to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital and underwent an operation for the removal of part of the left thumb and part of the left forefinger.
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation of two or more fingers at or near base, left hand

manifestations.description: the injury was painful for about 4 weeks after the accident and the pain was most severe at nights.
now he has no pain or feeling except when he knocks the stumps on something but then he experiences a very sharp acute pain followed by an ache for quite a long time.
good grip strength between the stump of the thumb and the 3rd finger and he exercises a 68 lbs grip with the right hand and a 40 1b grip with the left which is a good grip considering the amputations
there are two jobs that he finds he cannot do with his injuries, welding buttons and sewing padding in shoulders
The Plaintiff was granted a figure of 20% disability by the Medical assessment Board on the 27th July 1979.
Dr Wedderburn assesses the Plaintiff as having a 25% impairment of the whole man and the same permanent disability.

treatments_received: admitted to the Queen Elizabeth Hospital
operation for the removal of part of the left thumb and part of the left forefinger
operation carried out under local anaesthetic
attended daily for dressings for a further two weeks
wounds healed about six weeks after the accident
